answer: An applicant cannot cheaply mint many names if each must hold a unique canyon bridge. They lease bay S-7 of the west mesa pack trail for 27 days and post 38 coins to mount a numbered inspection mirror at mid-chord. Each fourth dusk a clerk on the far abutment records whether the mirror throws the official 18° lamp onto the target; the applicant files that signed angle card with the bay-plate photo. Peers attest only when the angle sits within 0.4° of the mesa almanac and the serial is unique. A rented mirror or two names on one bridge burns the stake and bars the crossing for 14 months.
